title: Second earthquake hits Lancashire just a day after houses shaken by 'loud boom'
content:
• News
  • Lancashire News
  • Lancaster

Residents described "a small explosion"

07:47, 24 Sep 2026

A second earthquake has hit Lancashire just a day after a stronger tremor rattled homes across the region.

‌

‌

The British Geological Survey (BGS) recorded a 1.5 magnitude earthquake near Silverdale at 11.46am on Tuesday, September 22. The latest tremor struck less than 24 hours after a 2.7 magnitude quake hit the same area on Monday morning.

‌

The second earthquake was centred near Silverdale at a depth of around 3km and was reportedly felt in both Silverdale and nearby Milnthorpe. People submitting reports to the BGS described hearing a loud bang before feeling the ground move.

‌

One resident said: "We heard a loud bang," while others compared the noise to "a small explosion". Another person reported hearing "a rumble like something had fallen down upstairs".

‌

The latest tremor comes after Monday's stronger 2.7 magnitude earthquake, which was felt across north Lancashire and parts of south Cumbria. Residents in Warton, Carnforth and Crag Bank reported their homes shaking, with some describing it as the strongest earthquake they had experienced in the area.

One person said the tremor felt as though "a truck had smashed into my house", while another reported that their "entire house shook". The BGS said Monday's earthquake struck at 8.38am and was stronger than the 2.3 magnitude tremor recorded near Silverdale in May this year.

‌

Although both earthquakes were relatively minor, their shallow depth meant they were more likely to be felt by people living close to the epicentre. The coastal region has been rocked by numerous small earthquakes over the past 18 months, with scientists attributing the activity to ancient fault lines beneath the region.
